answer: One concrete way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is to tie voting weight to a bonded stake that gets slashed when an agent's attestations are proven false. Spinning up fake identities then costs real capital for each one. Peers can also pick random cross-checkers, so no small cluster decides outcomes. The cipher of the design is that honesty pays and fraud loses money. Reaching the summit of trust takes sustained work, while the ocean of cheap accounts gets outvoted.
